A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, figures, equations and appendices. Existing material can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments, including generalization sweeps, attention ablations, RoPE experiments and head-pruning analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments on 2D images, three-object scenes, autoregressive generation and nonlinear-model attention.

M1.justification: The original CLIP procedure remains, but Appendix O adds an autoregressive architecture with frozen visual token embeddings, an MLP connector and a decoder trained by next-token prediction. Appendix N also adapts three-object contrastive training by selecting one valid caption and masking the other valid captions from negatives.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from one- and two-object 1D scenes to horizontal relations in 4×4 images and three-object scenes requiring simultaneous recovery of multiple relations (Appendices K and N). Appendix O additionally evaluates complete-caption generation.

E2.justification: Comparison variants expand within retained settings. Table 2 adds an EP+PP+BP ablation, whereas v1 Figure 5(e) used combined EP+PE+PP and EP+PE+PP+BP removals; it also adds ablated comparators to the previously unablated bidirectional experiment. No external baseline suite is introduced.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce substantive protocols: three-object training samples two configurations per triplet and evaluation measures top-1, mean correct relations in top-3, and complete top-3 recovery. Autoregressive evaluation requires free generation of the complete caption. The original 1D splits and retrieval criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix M adds bidirectional attention-term ablations and wrong-ordering failure analysis. Appendix N tests transfer from two-object training and performs three-object ablations. Appendices K, O and R add mechanistic checks in 2D, autoregressive and LayerNorm-containing models, substantially extending the original analyses.

E5.justification: Existing descriptive means and standard deviations across examples or positions are retained. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals or described significance tests.

E6.justification: New results include 98% unseen-pair accuracy on 2D images and 94% complete-caption generation accuracy in the autoregressive setting. Table 2 reports bidirectional top-2 accuracy falling from 92% to 64% under EP ablation; Table 4 reports three-object complete-relation recovery falling from 82% to 28%. These extend the results under specified conditions; the original result curves are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix R adds a bounded extension of the attention decomposition to LayerNorm: Equations 32–35 separate centered token, positional and bias contributions into nine terms, while acknowledging coupling through the normalization denominator. The existing positional-encoding and RoPE derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and three main contribution bullets retain the same central claims. The introduction and conclusion add applicability claims for autoregressive and nonlinear settings and three-object relations, while presenting the broader practical implications more cautiously.

C2.justification: The discussion newly distinguishes positional comparison from additive attribute factorization and simple role-conditioned codes. Added analyses explain incomplete transfer to three-object scenes and qualify the contributions of deeper layers. Appendix R explicitly limits its decomposition to first-layer analysis and acknowledges unresolved normalization coupling and validation.

D1.justification: Section 2.2 newly identifies AdamW. New Appendix B discloses A100/H100/H200 hardware, runtime and memory estimates, approximately 720 GPU-hours for main-text experiments, and upstream CLIP/grokking code provenance. These are additional disclosures, without evidence of a change to the original optimizer or computing setup.

R1.justification: The introduction and Sections 8–9 substantially expand positioning: encoder mechanisms are distinguished from downstream decoder improvements, and relational understanding from attribute factorization. Added discussions of Parascandolo, Uselis and mechanistic-interpretability work accompany a stronger claim that prior studies lack an ablation-supported spatial mechanism. Bibliographic publication updates are separate editorial changes.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites expand the motivation, related work and conclusion, rename Section 8.2, and add an Impact Statement and appendix sections. The existing section sequence and most original exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds four substantive multipanel figures (20, 22, 23 and 27) and three result tables (2–4). Numerous retained heatmaps have substantially higher resolution, improving legibility. Existing figures are relocated or renumbered, Figure 10 panel labels are corrected, and the existing mechanism-summary table becomes numbered Table 1.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central mechanistic argument beyond the original two-object analysis. Bidirectional and three-object ablations directly test its causal relevance, while transfer failures clarify its boundaries. The 2D, autoregressive and preliminary LayerNorm analyses address previously open applicability questions; sharper figures and computing disclosures improve assessability. Natural-image applicability and run-to-run uncertainty remain unresolved, but the added evidence materially improves the paper.
